More contact lets tuberculosis spread faster so fewer people stay in the vaccinated group.","analogy":"It is like a party where guests shake hands more often. A handshake is a chance for a germ to hop to a new person so a busier room spreads coughs much faster."},"intermediate":{"text":"The control is the contact rate called beta. The watched value is the number of vaccinated people called V. You move beta between half as much contact and twice as much contact. Raising beta makes people mix more so the disease pulls people out of the vaccinated compartment faster. Doubling the contact rate makes the peak of vaccinated people more than three million lower. This shows contact rate is a strong driver of protection."},"advanced":{"text":"The contact rate beta enters the effective reproduction number for the SVEITRS tuberculosis model.
